title: Artinian local algebras with finite H_1 of the residue field are filtered colimits of flat essentially finite type ones
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $(\Lambda,\mathfrak m,K)$ be an Artinian local $k$-algebra (a commutative $k$-algebra which is a local ring, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and residue field $K=\Lambda/\mathfrak m$, in which every descending chain of ideals is eventually constant). Assume that $H_1(L_{K/k})$, the first homology of the naive cotangent complex of the $k$-algebra $K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], is a finite dimensional $K$-vector space. Then there is a set $\mathcal A$ of $k$-subalgebras $A\subseteq\Lambda$, directed under inclusion (any two members are contained in a third) and with union $\Lambda$, such that every $A\in\mathcal A$ is an Artinian local ring, the inclusion $A\to\Lambda$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $\mathfrak m_A\Lambda=\mathfrak m$ (the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ of $A$ generates the ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $\Lambda$), and $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] (isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to a localization $W^{-1}B$ of a finitely generated $k$-algebra $B$ at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$). In particular $\Lambda$ is the filtered colimit of the Artinian local $k$-algebras $A\in\mathcal A$, with flat maps $A\to\Lambda$, $\mathfrak m_A\Lambda=\mathfrak m$, and $A$ essentially of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, line 2444), Section 07FF (section-inseparable); its proof (lines 2455-2549) uses Algebra Lemmas 0320 (formally smooth extensions of F_p), 07DT (essentially of finite type into Artinian local) and the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p in k in K

proof.text: *Setup.* By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] $\Lambda$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\mathfrak m^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$; so $\mathfrak m$ is a finitely generated ideal: choose $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d\in\mathfrak m$ generating it. The structure map $i:k\to\Lambda$ is injective ($k$ is a field and $\Lambda\neq0$), so $p\cdot1_\Lambda=0$; the composite $k\to\Lambda\to K$ is injective as well, and we regard $k$ as a subfield of $K$ through it. For a ring homomorphism $\sigma:K\to\Lambda$ with $\sigma(c)\bmod\mathfrak m=c$ for all $c\in K$ (a section of $\Lambda\to K$) let $\Psi_\sigma:K[x_1,\dots,x_d]\to\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] be the ring homomorphism which is $\sigma$ on coefficients and sends $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$; for a subfield $F\subseteq K$ write $\Psi_\sigma(F[x])$ for the image of $F[x_1,\dots,x_d]$, a subring of $\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2455-2470: 'Let n be the minimal integer such that m^n = 0', 'Pick lambda_1, ..., lambda_d in m which generate m', definition of Psi_sigma)

proof.text: *The claim, and its base case.* Claim $(C_n)$, for $n\ge1$: for every commutative local $k$-algebra $(\Lambda,\mathfrak m,K)$ with $\mathfrak m^n=0$ and every finite family $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$ generating $\mathfrak m$ (with $\Psi_\sigma$ as in step 1), there are a section $\sigma:K\to\Lambda$ of $\Lambda\to K$ which is a ring homomorphism and a subfield $k\subseteq F\subseteq K$ finitely generated over $k$ (generated as a field by $k$ and finitely many elements) [def-pc-field-extension] such that $i(k)\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(F[x])$. We prove $(C_n)$ by induction on $n$. For $n=1$, $\mathfrak m=0$ and $\Lambda=K$; take $\sigma=\mathrm{id}_K$ and $F=k$: then $\Psi_\sigma(k[x])=k=i(k)$ (all $\lambda_i=0$). Steps 3-7 prove $(C_n)$ for $n\ge2$ assuming $(C_{n-1})$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2471-2477: 'Claim: there exists a sigma ... We will prove the claim by induction ... It is clear for n = 1')

proof.text: *Inductive step: lifting $\sigma'$ and $\tau'$.* Let $n\ge2$, $I=\mathfrak m^{n-1}$, $\Lambda'=\Lambda/I$, a local $k$-algebra with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak m/I$, $\mathfrak m'^{n-1}=0$, residue field $K$, $\mathfrak m'$ generated by the images $\lambda'_i$ of the $\lambda_i$. Since $2(n-1)\ge n$, $I^2=0$; and $\mathfrak mI=\mathfrak m^n=0$, so $I$ is a $K$-vector space through $\Lambda\to K$. By $(C_{n-1})$ there are a section $\sigma':K\to\Lambda'$ and $k\subseteq F'\subseteq K$ finitely generated with $i'(k)\subseteq A':=\Psi_{\sigma'}(F'[x])$, $i':k\to\Lambda'$ the structure map; let $\tau':k\to A'$ be $i'$ with target $A'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] (field $K$, $D=\Lambda$, $J=I$) there is a ring homomorphism $\sigma:K\to\Lambda$ lifting $\sigma'$; it is a section of $\Lambda\to K$. Put $\bar A=F'[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)^n$; as $\lambda^E=\lambda_1^{e_1}\cdots\lambda_d^{e_d}\in\mathfrak m^n=0$ for $|E|=n$, $\Psi_\sigma$ induces $\Psi_\sigma:\bar A\to\Lambda$, and $\bar A\to\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ equals the map induced by $\Psi_{\sigma'}$ (as $\sigma$ lifts $\sigma'$), so it maps $\bar A$ onto $A'$. $\bar A$ is local with nilpotent maximal ideal $(x)/(x)^n$ (an element $c+h$, $c\in F'^\times$, $h\in(x)$, is a unit, $h$ being nilpotent), and $A'\neq0$, so the kernel $J$ of $\bar A\to A'$ lies in $(x)/(x)^n$ and $J^n=0$; also $p\cdot1_{\bar A}=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-nilpotent-lifting] (field $k$, $D=\bar A$, $J$) there is a ring homomorphism $\tau:k\to\bar A$ lifting $\tau'$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2479-2497: 'If n > 1 set I = m^{n-1} ... Choose a lift sigma : K -> Lambda of sigma' ... Set A = F[x_1, ..., x_d]/(x_1, ..., x_d)^n ... Choose a lift tau : k -> A of tau''; Stacks writes F for F' here and invokes formal smoothness of K/F_p and k/F_p, Algebra 0320, for lifts along the nilpotent kernels)

proof.text: *The derivation $\theta$ and the effect of changing $\sigma$.* Let $\theta=i-\Psi_\sigma\circ\tau:k\to\Lambda$. Modulo $I$ both $i$ and $\Psi_\sigma\circ\tau$ reduce to $i'$ (the second is $\Psi_{\sigma'}\circ\tau'=i'$), so $\theta$ takes values in $I$. It is additive, and for $a,b\in k$: $\theta(ab)=i(a)i(b)-\psi(a)\psi(b)=i(a)\theta(b)+\psi(b)\theta(a)$ with $\psi=\Psi_\sigma\circ\tau$; since $i(a)-\bar a$ and $\psi(b)-\bar b$ act as zero on $I$ ($\mathfrak mI=0$; here $\bar a$ is the image of $a$ in $K$ acting on the $K$-vector space $I$), $\theta(ab)=a\theta(b)+b\theta(a)$: $\theta$ is a derivation of $k$ into the $k$-module $I$, an $\mathbf F_p$-derivation (it kills $1$, hence the image of $\mathbf F_p$) [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $D:K\to I$ be any derivation (additive, $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$). Then $\sigma+D:K\to\Lambda$ is again a ring homomorphism lifting $\sigma'$: $(\sigma+D)(ab)=\sigma(a)\sigma(b)+\sigma(a)D(b)+\sigma(b)D(a)$, as $D(a)D(b)\in I^2=0$ and $\sigma(a)$ acts on $I$ as $a$. For $a\in k$ write $\tau(a)=\sum_Ec_Ex^E$ with $c_E\in F'$; then $\Psi_{\sigma+D}(\tau(a))=\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))+\sum_ED(c_E)\lambda^E=\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))+D(c_0)$, since $D(c_E)\lambda^E\in I\mathfrak m=0$ for $|E|\ge1$; and $c_0=\bar a$, because $\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))\bmod\mathfrak m=c_0$ and $\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))\equiv i(a)$ modulo $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Hence replacing $\sigma$ by $\sigma+D$ (and keeping $\tau$) replaces $\theta$ by $\theta-D|_k$, $D|_k$ the composite $k\subseteq K\xrightarrow{D}I$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2490-2500: 'These maps agree modulo I, whence the difference is a derivation theta = i - Psi_sigma o tau : k -> I. Note that if we change sigma into sigma + D then we change theta into theta - D|_k'

proof.text: *Jacobi-Zariski for $\mathbf F_p\subseteq k\subseteq K$ and the finite set $J_0$.* $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is spanned over $k$ by the $\mathrm dy$, $y\in k$, so it has a $k$-basis of the form $(\mathrm dy_j)_{j\in J}$, $y_j\in k$ (a spanning set of a vector space contains a basis); then $(1\otimes\mathrm dy_j)_{j\in J}$ is a $K$-basis of $K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] for $\mathbf F_p\to k\to K$ the sequence $H_1(L_{K/k})\xrightarrow{\partial}K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$, $w(c\otimes\mathrm db)=c\,\mathrm db$, is exact ($H_1$ as in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]). By hypothesis $H_1(L_{K/k})$ is finite dimensional, so $\ker w=\operatorname{im}\partial$ is finite dimensional; each vector of a finite basis of it is a finite combination of the $1\otimes\mathrm dy_j$, so there is a finite $J_0\subseteq J$ with $\ker w\subseteq\bigoplus_{j\in J_0}K(1\otimes\mathrm dy_j)$. Then the elements $w(1\otimes\mathrm dy_j)=\mathrm dy_j\in\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$, $j\in J\setminus J_0$, are $K$-linearly independent: if $\sum_{j\notin J_0}c_j\,\mathrm dy_j=0$ (finite sum) then $\sum_{j\notin J_0}c_j\otimes\mathrm dy_j\in\ker w\subseteq\bigoplus_{J_0}K(1\otimes\mathrm dy_j)$, so all $c_j=0$ by linear independence of the basis. (Stacks also uses $H_1(L_{K/\mathbf F_p})=0$ to write the sequence starting with $0$; only exactness at $K\otimes_k\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ is needed.)

The Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p in k in K is ... we can find a finite subset J_0 ... Hence the elements dy_j, j in J minus J_0 map to K-linearly independent elements')

otin J_0$, are $K$-linearly independent in $\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}$ (step 5), extend them to a $K$-basis and let $\delta:\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}	o I$ be a $K$-linear map with $\delta(\mathrm dy_j)= ar	heta(\mathrm dy_j)$ for $j
otin J_0$ (and, say, $0$ on the other basis vectors). Then $D:=\delta\circ\mathrm d:K	o I$ is a derivation, and $D|_k(a)=\delta(\mathrm da)$ for $a\in k$. proof.text: *End of the induction.* $I=\mathfrak m^{n-1}$ is generated as an ideal by the monomials $\lambda^E$, $|E|=n-1$ (as $\mathfrak m=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d)$), and $\mathfrak mI=0$, so $I=\sum_{|E|=n-1}\sigma(K)\lambda^E$; write $f_j=\sum_{|E|=n-1}\sigma(c_{j,E})\lambda^E$ with $c_{j,E}\in K$ ($j\in J_0$), and let $F=F'(c_{j,E}:j\in J_0,|E|=n-1)$, finitely generated over $k$ ($J_0$ is finite). For $a\in k$, $i(a)=\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))+\sum_{j\in J_0}i(a_j)f_j$ (step 6). First, $\tau(a)\in\bar A=F'[x]/(x)^n$, so $\Psi_\sigma(\tau(a))\in\Psi_\sigma(F'[x])\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(F[x])$. Second, $i(a_j)$ acts on $I$ as $\bar a_j\in k\subseteq F$, so $i(a_j)f_j=\sum_E\sigma(\bar a_jc_{j,E})\lambda^E=\Psi_\sigma\bigl(\sum_E\bar a_jc_{j,E}x^E\bigr)\in\Psi_\sigma(F[x])$. Hence $i(k)\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(F[x])$, which is $(C_n)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2531-2537: 'Note that I is generated by the monomials lambda^E of total degree n-1 ... Write f_j = sum c_{j,E} lambda^E with c_{j,E} in K. Replace F' by F = F'(c_{j,E}). Then the claim holds.')

proof.text: *Presentation of $\Lambda$.* Apply $(C_n)$ (steps 2-7) to $\Lambda$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$ of step 1: we get $\sigma$ and $F_1$ with $i(k)\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(F_1[x])$. $\Psi_\sigma:K[x_1,\dots,x_d]\to\Lambda$ is surjective: $\Lambda=\sigma(K)+\mathfrak m$, and inductively $\Lambda=\Psi_\sigma(K[x])+\mathfrak m^r$ for all $r\ge1$, because $\mathfrak m^r=\sum_{|E|=r}\lambda^E\Lambda=\sum_{|E|=r}\lambda^E(\sigma(K)+\mathfrak m)\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(K[x])+\mathfrak m^{r+1}$; take $r=n$. $K[x_1,\dots,x_d]$ is of finite type over the field $K$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so $\ker\Psi_\sigma$ is generated by finitely many $g_1,\dots,g_t$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $F_0=F_1(\text{coefficients of }g_1,\dots,g_t)$, finitely generated over $k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be the set of subfields $F_0\subseteq F\subseteq K$ finitely generated over $k$ [def-pc-field-extension]. For $F\in\mathcal F$ put $A_F=\Psi_\sigma(F[x])\subseteq\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2539-2543: 'Choose sigma and F as in the claim. The kernel of Psi_sigma is generated by finitely many polynomials g_1, ..., g_t in K[x_1, ..., x_d] and we may assume their coefficients are in F after enlarging F'; surjectivity of Psi_sigma, used in 'K[x_1,...,x_d]/(g_1,...,g_t) = Lambda', is written out here)

proof.text: *$A_F\to\Lambda$ is flat.* Let $F\in\mathcal F$ and $B_F=F[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)$, an $F$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (for $F[x]\to K[x]$ and the ideal $(g_1,\dots,g_t)$) and $K\otimes_FF[x]=K[x]$, $B_F\otimes_FK\cong K[x]/(g_1,\dots,g_t)K[x]=K[x]/\ker\Psi_\sigma\cong\Lambda$, and the composite $B_F\to B_F\otimes_FK\cong\Lambda$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, is the map $\bar\Psi$ induced by $\Psi_\sigma|_{F[x]}$ (which kills the $g_j$). By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] (field extension $K/F$, $D=B_F$) $B_F\to B_F\otimes_FK$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], hence injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] (case $I=0$). So $\bar\Psi:B_F\to\Lambda$ is injective with image $A_F$, i.e. $B_F\cong A_F$, and the inclusion $A_F\to\Lambda$, identified with $B_F\to B_F\otimes_FK$, is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2543-2546: 'In this case it is clear that the map A = F[x_1, ..., x_d]/(g_1, ..., g_t) -> K[x_1, ..., x_d]/(g_1, ..., g_t) = Lambda is flat'; the injectivity is in the first sentence of the proof, line 2456)

proof.text: *$A_F$ is an Artinian local $k$-subalgebra with $\mathfrak m_{A_F}\Lambda=\mathfrak m$ and residue field $F$.* $A_F$ is a subring of $\Lambda$ containing $i(k)$, since $i(k)\subseteq\Psi_\sigma(F_1[x])\subseteq A_F$ (step 8); so it is a $k$-subalgebra and $A_F\to\Lambda$ a $k$-algebra map. As $\lambda^E=0$ for $|E|=n$, $A_F$ is the image of $F[x]/(x)^n$, a finite dimensional $F$-algebra (through $\sigma|_F$), hence Artinian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian]. Every element of $A_F$ is $\sigma(c)+h$ with $c\in F$, $h\in\mathfrak n:=\Psi_\sigma((x)F[x])=\sum_i\lambda_iA_F$; $h$ is nilpotent ($h\in\mathfrak m$), so $\sigma(c)+h$ is a unit of $A_F$ when $c\neq0$ ($\sigma(c)^{-1}=\sigma(c^{-1})\in A_F$), while $\mathfrak n\subseteq\mathfrak m$ consists of non-units. So $A_F$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{A_F}=\mathfrak n=A_F\cap\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak m_{A_F}\Lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d)\Lambda=\mathfrak m$, and $A_F/\mathfrak m_{A_F}\to\Lambda/\mathfrak m=K$ is injective with image $F$; the composite $k\to A_F\to A_F/\mathfrak m_{A_F}\cong F$ is the inclusion $k\subseteq F$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2546-2547: 'By the claim A is a k-subalgebra of Lambda'; Artinian local and m_A Lambda = m are not argued in Stacks)

proof.text: *$A_F$ is essentially of finite type over $k$.* Write $F=k(a_1,\dots,a_r)$. The $k$-subalgebra $B=k[a_1,\dots,a_r]\subseteq F$ is of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and a domain; with $W=B\setminus\{0\}$, the $k$-algebra map $W^{-1}B\to F$, $b/w\mapsto bw^{-1}$, is injective ($F$ is a field, $B$ a domain) and surjective (its image is a subfield containing $k$ and the $a_i$). So $k\to F$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. By step 10, $F$ is the residue field of the Artinian local ring $A_F$ and $k\to A_F\to A_F/\mathfrak m_{A_F}$ is $k\subseteq F$; by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-essentially-finite-type-residue] $k\to A_F$ is essentially of finite type.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FG (lemma-helper, lines 2548-2550: 'Finally, these algebras are essentially of finite type over k by Algebra, Lemma 07DT'

proof.text: *The directed union.* Let $\mathcal A=\{A_F:F\in\mathcal F\}$. By steps 9-11 each $A_F$ has the required properties. $\mathcal F$ is directed: for $F,F'\in\mathcal F$ the compositum $FF'$ (generated by $F_0$ and the finitely many generators of both) lies in $\mathcal F$, and $F\subseteq F'$ implies $A_F\subseteq A_{F'}$; so $\mathcal A$ is directed under inclusion. Every element of $\Lambda$ is $\Psi_\sigma(h)$ for some $h\in K[x]$ (step 8); with $F=F_0(\text{coefficients of }h)\in\mathcal F$ it lies in $A_F$. So $\Lambda=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal A}A$, and $\Lambda$ is the filtered colimit of the system $\mathcal A$ with the inclusions as transition maps.
